tool_description: Integrate with VS Code extension for AI-powered code editing with project awareness

available_commands.description: Send edit instruction to VS Code (default command)
Fetch file contents from VS Code
Verify changes were applied to file
List files currently open in VS Code
Check VS Code extension connection status
Search the codebase for text, a function name, or a filename. mode must be 'text' (default), 'function', or 'file'. root defaults to '.'.
Get the folder and file structure of the project. root defaults to '.', max_depth defaults to 3.
Replace a specific line range (1-indexed, inclusive) with new_content. Use instead of full-file rewrites for targeted edits. ALWAYS fetch the file first to confirm line numbers.

tool_usage_examples: {"tool": "coding.edit", "args": ["add error handling following the pattern in utils.py", "main.py"]}
tool_usage_guidance: STEP 1: On a new task, run coding.tree first to understand the project structure
STEP 2: Use coding.search to locate the relevant file and function before touching anything
STEP 3: ALWAYS fetch the target file (or the specific line range) before editing or patching
STEP 4: Prefer coding.patch over coding.edit for targeted changes — patch replaces exact lines, reducing errors
STEP 5: Use coding.verify after any edit or patch to confirm the change is present
Use coding.search mode='text' to find any string or keyword across all source files
Use coding.search mode='function' to locate where a function is defined (searches def/function keywords)
Use coding.search mode='file' to find files by name without scanning their contents
Use coding.tree to orient yourself in an unfamiliar project before asking questions
Use coding.patch when you know the exact lines to replace — always fetch first to confirm line numbers
Use coding.edit for natural-language instructions when exact line numbers are unknown
FILE PATHS: Use relative paths from project root (e.g., 'api/routes.py', 'services/db.py')
CONTEXT: Check personality/base_memory/base_personality/coding_context.py for project structure and conventions
SESSION FILES: Ask user to upload key project files (routes, models, config, types) as Session Files before coding
PATTERNS: Ask 'should I follow the same pattern as [related_file]?' before making style or structure choices
Empty command defaults to 'edit' for convenience
Requires VS Code with Ollama Code Editor extension running on localhost:3000
proactive_triggers: When user starts a new coding task — run coding.tree FIRST to understand project structure
When user mentions a function name — use coding.search mode='function' to locate it before editing
When user requests code changes or modifications — FETCH FILE FIRST, then patch or edit
When debugging or fixing bugs in code
When adding new features to existing code
When refactoring code for better structure
When user mentions specific files by name — search for the file if path is uncertain
When user asks to see or review file contents — use coding.fetch
When user describes project structure — ask to help set up coding_context.py
When user uploads files — check if they want to populate coding_context.py with file mappings
When user wants consistency — fetch related files to identify project patterns first

metadata.notes: Requires VS Code with Ollama Code Editor extension. Extension runs HTTP server on localhost:3000 by default. v3.0.0 adds search (text/function/file), tree (project structure), and patch (targeted line-range edits).

coding_best_practices.orient_first: Run coding.tree at the start of any new task to understand the project layout
coding_best_practices.search_before_edit: Use coding.search to find the right file and function before making any changes
coding_best_practices.fetch_first: Always fetch the target file (or line range) before editing or patching
coding_best_practices.patch_over_edit: Prefer coding.patch for targeted changes — it replaces exact line ranges and is less error-prone than full rewrites
coding_best_practices.context_matters: Use coding_context.py from base_memory to provide file mappings and coding conventions
coding_best_practices.relative_paths: Use paths relative to project root; ask user for root directory if uncertain
coding_best_practices.describe_edits: In edit instructions, mention project patterns, naming conventions, and architectural decisions
coding_best_practices.session_files: Ask users to upload key project files (routes, models, config, types) as Session Files before coding
coding_best_practices.verify_changes: After any edit or patch, use coding.verify to confirm the change is present
coding_best_practices.ask_about_patterns: Always ask 'should I follow the same pattern as [related file]?' before making style choices

metadata.context_loading: On startup, load personality/base_memory/base_personality/coding_context.py to get project structure and conventions
